   STAFF REPORT

Meeting Date:  September 4, 2024
To:  Community Security Ad Hoc Liaisons Honorable Mayor & Council
  Member Corman
From:  Stephanie Harris, Director of Community Services
  Chad Lynn, Deputy Director Special Projects Public Safety
Subject:  Safety and Hospitality Services
Attachments:  Ambassador Agreement

INTRODUCTION
The current Safety and Hospitality service agreement with Mydatt, DBA Block by Block
expires March 31, 2025. Staff is seeking direction from the Community Security Ad Hoc
on the focus and scope of these services and methods for service delivery.
Since the execution of the original Safety and Hospitality Services Agreement, the City
has expanded its own operations, services, and service provider agreements to include
additional resources supporting a variety of outreach and public safety needs. This
includes two trained police officers and a Department of Mental Health Clinician as part
of the Mental Health Evaluation Team (MHET) deployed through the Police Department,
and the expanded Beverly Hills Outreach Team (BHOT) contracted with Step Up on
Second, with 5 Outreach members working 7 days a week to assist with Homeless
Outreach services. The City has also engaged private security companies to assist with
community safety throughout the City. With the expansion of these programs and
services, it is requested that the Community Security Ad Hoc provide direction on the
scope of work related specifically to the Safety and Hospitality Agreement.
DISCUSSION
Following the success of the Ambassador pilot program during the 2015-2016 fiscal
year, City Council agreed to provide funding for a one-year plan for a total not-to-exceed
$500,000 for fiscal year 2016-2017. This one-year plan included 21-hour daily staffing
with a total of 10 full-time equivalent employees focused in the business triangle and
addressing social service needs.

The program has since evolved, and the Ambassadors continue to have significant
positive impact on the community. Today, Ambassadors provide 21.20 full-time
equivalent employees for 24-hour services. These services include distribution of
hospitality and local events information, safety escorts, parking garage sweeps,
homeless engagement, Tour Bus loading, and education on smoking regulations.
Services are provided in the City's business triangle, South Beverly Drive from Wilshire

Boulevard to Gregory Way, and other designated areas such as the City’s parking
garages and Beverly Canon Gardens.

The Ambassadors also collaborate closely with the City’s historic and expanded service
providers, including BHOT, MHET, Nastec, and Park Rangers.

As part of the Joint Powers Agreement (JPA) with the Beverly Hills Unified School
District, Ambassadors provide field permit and facility management at Beverly Hills High
School, Beverly Vista Middle School, El Rodeo Elementary School, and Horace Mann
Elementary School. These services are currently funded by the City and in addition to
JPA funding. The Ambassadors only supplement the District security staff, and are
focused on facilitating access and availability for City programs held at the schools. Per
the JPA, the overall security of District facilities continues to be the responsibility of the
District.

As the scope of services for the Ambassador program has continued to expand, the
funding for this program has also grown from the initial $500,000 in 2016 to
approximately $1.4 million in fiscal year 2023-2024. The increase in funding accounts for
the expansion of the program, and general inflationary costs associated with uniforms
and salary increases. For the year 2024-2025, Block by Block was awarded a partial
year, 9-month agreement for $1.2 million pending the Ad Hoc’s direction related to the
ongoing service and scope of work of the Ambassador program.

FISCAL IMPACT
No fiscal impact at this time.

RECOMMENDATION
Based on the direction from the Ad Hoc, staff will be prepared to release a Request for
Proposals (RFP) using the current or modified scope of work to secure services under a
new multi-year agreement or return to the Ad Hoc Committee with additional information
and/or options for carrying out the desired services.

  Stephanie Harris,
  Director of Community Services
  Approved By
